Personal Information
Name: Alok Ranjan

University: IIT Madras
Degree Program: B.S. in Data Science
Year of Study: First Year
Title
AI-Powered Log Triage and Security Alert Aggregator for Fedora
Synopsis
This project aims to build an AI-powered tool that collects, parses, classifies, and prioritizes
security-relevant logs on a Fedora system. It will aggregate data from multiple sources such as
SELinux, audit logs, and systemd journal, then apply lightweight machine learning/NLP
techniques to detect and elevate critical alerts while suppressing routine messages. This will
improve system administrator efficiency and response times.
Benefits to the Community
This project enhances the Fedora ecosystem by:
● Providing a modern AI-based triage system for security logs
● Reducing noise and surfacing critical alerts quickly
● Improving incident response for Fedora users and system administrators
● Offering an extensible platform that can evolve with newer AI models

sections.heading: Page 2
sections.content:
The tool will help Fedora stand out as a security-conscious distro with intelligent log handling.
Deliverables
1. Source Code Repository: Python/Bash scripts, ML models, and log parsing logic.
2. Packaged RPM: A user-installable package for Fedora.
3. Documentation: Installation, configuration, usage, developer guide.
4. Prototype/CLI: Real-time demo showcasing live classification and prioritization.
5. Testing & Evaluation: Unit/integration tests, model benchmarks.
Timeline
Community Bonding
● Connect with mentor and Fedora community
● Research log formats (SELinux, journalctl, audit)
● Finalize model scope (rule-based + ML hybrid approach)
Week 1–2
● Setup dev environment and test data pipelines
● Write log collectors for systemd journal and SELinux
Week 3–4
● Develop initial parsing and preprocessing pipeline
● Start with rule-based classifier (regexes, basic heuristics)

sections.heading: Page 3
sections.content:
Week 5–7
● Introduce ML pipeline (scikit-learn baseline: Naive Bayes/SVM)
● Create CLI prototype with real-time classification
● Write unit tests for pipeline and model evaluation
Midterm Evaluation
● Functional log triage system with basic ML
● Working CLI to test on simulated log files
Week 8–10
● Expand model with NLP (simple LSTM or Transformer via PyTorch/Tensorflow)
● Add noise filtering and priority scoring logic
Week 11–12
● Package tool as RPM
● Write documentation and final test coverage
● Prepare final report and showcase demo
Technical Approach
● Log Collection: Use journalctl, ausearch, and SELinux audit tools to gather logs.
● Preprocessing: Normalize timestamps, extract fields, clean text.
● Modeling:
○ Start with rules/regexes for known log patterns

sections.heading: Page 4
sections.content:
○ Add ML-based classification (supervised model trained on labeled log types)
○ Optional: Enhance with BERT/LSTM for NLP-based classification
● Packaging: RPM with scripts and dependencies
● Testing: Unit tests with pytest, performance evaluation using recall/precision
About Me
I am an engineering student from India with strong backend experience in Python, Bash
scripting, and system-level Linux work. I'm actively learning AI/ML, security, and automation.
I've built OCR tools in Rust and backend systems in Django. This project aligns with both my
interests and skillset — particularly Linux internals, AI, and security.
Why Fedora & GSoC
Fedora is a bleeding-edge distro that emphasizes open standards and community. Working with
Fedora will allow me to contribute meaningfully to security tooling and sharpen my skills in
real-world environments. GSoC offers the ideal structure and mentorship to bring this idea to
life.
Future Scope
● Add GUI for real-time log dashboards
● Integrate with SIEM tools (e.g., Wazuh, Splunk)
● Add support for network-based logs (syslog, rsyslog)
● Enable automated remediation for high-severity alerts
